name: 常驻 PowerShell
description: 给 Agent 的 PowerShell 快速通道：常驻一个 pwsh 进程，每条命令在独立 Runspace 中执行，省掉每次约 250ms 的 pwsh 冷启动，轻量命令单次耗时从约 440ms 降到约 60ms。语义与内置 Bash 对齐：同样接受 PowerShell 语法、同样的工作目录（工作区根）、退出码按 $? 判定。状态隔离，变量与函数不跨命令残留。任何 daemon 故障都会返回 fallback 让模型改回内置 Bash；不联网、不读项目文件、不碰凭据。

en.name: Resident PowerShell
en.description: A PowerShell fast lane for the agent: one resident pwsh process, with each command executed in its own Runspace, removing the ~250ms pwsh cold start so short commands drop from about 440ms to about 60ms. Semantics match the built-in Bash tool: same PowerShell syntax, same working directory (the workspace root), and $?-based exit codes. State is isolated, so variables and functions never leak between commands. Any daemon failure returns fallback so the model switches back to the built-in Bash tool. No network, no project file reads, no credentials.
en.safetyNotes: The plugin spawns only its own bundled server.ps1 through the local pwsh executable, and speaks a line-delimited base64+JSON protocol over stdio. Each command runs in a fresh Runspace, so no state carries over between commands. The registered tool takes a PowerShell command string, an optional working directory and an optional timeout; output is capped at 8MB and truncated with a note rather than hanging. The daemon is a child process of the app with no pipe or port reachable from outside.

agentTools.name: pwsh_run
agentTools.description: Run a PowerShell command in a resident daemon instead of spawning pwsh each time. This is the fast lane for PowerShell: it costs about 60ms instead of the ~440ms a fresh `pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command` start takes, so it is roughly 7-10x faster for short commands. It is a drop-in replacement for the Bash tool on this Windows host: same PowerShell syntax, same exit-code semantics ($? based, matching `pwsh -Command`), same working directory (the workspace root). Each command runs in a fresh Runspace, so variables/functions do NOT leak between calls. Use it for Get-ChildItem, Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object, Get-Content, Test-Path, Get-Item, $env: reads, and ordinary native commands (git/node/cmd). Use the Bash tool instead for commands whose exit code must be exactly propagated (this tool maps `exit N` to 1), long builds and test suites, and anything interactive. If the result has fallback=true, do NOT retry here: call the Bash tool instead.

command.description: The PowerShell command to run, e.g. 'Get-ChildItem -File | Select-Object -First 5'. Same syntax as the Bash tool.

cwd.description: Optional working directory. Defaults to the current workspace root.

timeoutMs.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (1000-600000). Defaults to 60000.
